sections.history: Koodal is the ancient poetic name of Madurai, and Koodal Azhagar — 'the beautiful one of Koodal' — is the city's own Divya Desam, standing a short walk from the Meenakshi Amman temple. It is one of the 108 Divya Desams of the Pandya Nadu, and it holds a special place in Sri Vaishnava memory as the shrine linked with Periyalvar, the Alvar of Srivilliputhur and foster-father of Andal. Tradition holds that it was here, before the Pandya court, that he sang the Thiruppallandu, the benediction with which the recitation of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham still begins. The temple grew under the Pandyas and later the Madurai Nayaks, and remains a busy place of worship in the old city.
sections.architecture: The temple is famous for its Ashtanga vimana, a tower built in three storeys, each with its own form of Vishnu: the lord seated as Koodal Azhagar in the sanctum below, standing as Surya Narayana above, and reclining on the serpent at the top level, a shrine devotees may climb to see. The Goddess Mathuravalli Thayar has her own shrine. Unusually for a Vishnu temple, a shrine of the nine planets stands within the precincts.
sections.legends: The sthala purana tells of the Pandya king Vallabhadeva, who walked the city in disguise to learn the lives of his people and, moved by a pilgrim's words, sought to know who was the supreme god. He called the learned to debate, and Periyalvar, a simple garland-maker of Srivilliputhur, proved the supremacy of Vishnu. As the king led him through Madurai in honour, Vishnu appeared in the sky on Garuda; and Periyalvar, fearing the evil eye might fall on such beauty, burst into song — 'Pallandu, pallandu', may you live for countless years.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the great Vaishnava festivals, above all Vaikunta Ekadashi, when the gateway of heaven is opened and the old city fills with devotees. Processions of the utsava deities through the surrounding streets, and the recitation of Thiruppallandu in the shrine where it is said to have been born, are highlights of its year.
sections.experience: Koodal Azhagar is easily reached from the Meenakshi temple and is best visited unhurried. After darshan of the seated lord, climb the vimana to see the standing and reclining forms in turn — a rare chance to circle a sanctum tower from within. It pairs naturally with Kallazhagar and Thirumohur on a day among Madurai's Divya Desams.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; Vaikunta Ekadashi is very crowded. Confirm current timings, including access to the upper vimana shrines, before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: The temple stands in central Madurai, south-west of the Meenakshi Amman temple and close to the Periyar bus stand, reachable on foot or by auto-rickshaw. Madurai Junction railway station is nearby, and Madurai Airport lies about 12 km south.
